english.title: Protest outside of public office-holder's home
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) carried on a protest outside, or in the vicinity of premises at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION OF PREMISES..) that were used as a dwelling by **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a **(..SPECIFY OFFICE HOLDER..), for the purpose of representing to, or persuading, the public office-holder that they should or should not do something or should have or should not have done something and carried on the protest because of, or in connection with, the public officer-holder being a public officer-holder
english.legislation: Contrary to section 162 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026.

english.notes:
(i) Protest activity is not linked to a specific future or past action, ensuring that harassing or intimidatory protests outside homes of individuals are captured, regardless of whether they relate to past or future conduct. (ii) The offence does not carry a harassment requirement. Parliament considers any protest outside of the home of a public office-holder is by default, regarded as harassment.
(iii) For the meanings of “Public office-holder” and “Official residence” see section 162(8) and (11).
(iv) “Dwelling” has the meaning provided by section 8 of the Public Order Act 1986.
(v) The offence applies to any premises used as a private residence by a public office-holder including a residential constituency or London address. However, as per section 162(1) the offence does not apply official residences, preserving the right to protest in public political spaces (for example, near Number 10 Downing Street); nor would it apply to constituency offices.
(vi) A defence will be available to persons charged with this offence when demonstrated that they did not know the premises were used by the public office-holder as a dwelling (section 162(3)).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level 4 on the standard scale. The maximum penalty depends on the maximum term for summary offences. For offences committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force this is 6 months, for offences committed on or after that date 51 weeks.
